cli.usage:
Usage: siplink <command> [arguments]

Commands:
  serve                          Start the platform (default)
  admin create [--super] [--region name]... [--name display-name] <username>
                                 Create an administrator; prints a one-time password
  admin reset-password <username>
                                 Reset an administrator's password; prints a one-time password
  admin reset-2fa <username>     Delete an administrator's two-step methods and recovery codes
  pki show                       Show the certificate mode, built-in CA, server and own certificates
  pki export-ca <path>           Export the built-in CA certificate (PEM)
  pki renew                      Reissue the server certificate now (not while issuing is paused)
  pki import [--yes] <chain-file> <key-file>
                                 Use an own certificate (PEM, server certificate first); --yes after notices
  pki use-builtin [--yes]        Stop using the own certificate, return to the built-in CA
  seed <spec-file.json>          Create or update test data from a spec; print the client's binding URL
  backup <target-file>           Back up the database to a file (back up the key file separately)
  health                         Check the local HTTP(S) service (Docker health check)
  migrate                        Run the database migrations only
  version                        Show the version
cli.admin.subcommand: admin needs a subcommand: create, reset-password, reset-2fa
cli.admin.create_usage: Usage: siplink admin create [--super] [--region name]... [--name display-name] <username>
cli.admin.username_invalid: The user name must be 2–32 letters, digits or . _ -
cli.admin.region_needed: A region administrator needs at least one --region; for a super administrator add --super
cli.admin.change_on_login: The password must be changed at the first sign-in.
cli.admin.password_reset_after: All sessions of this administrator have ended; the password must be changed at the next sign-in.
cli.admin.two_step_reset_after: All methods and recovery codes are deleted; all sessions of this administrator have ended.
cli.pki.subcommand: pki needs a subcommand: show, export-ca, renew, import, use-builtin
cli.pki.renewed: Server certificate reissued; the running platform uses it within a minute.
cli.pki.issuing: Automatic issuing by the built-in CA:
cli.pki.issuing_running: Running (renews when fewer than 30 days are left or the names change)
cli.pki.qr_pin_none: None (devices check against the Android system CAs)
cli.pki.trust_public: Public CA (devices check against the Android system CAs)
cli.pki.trust_none: Not trusted by a public CA, and the chain holds no root certificate
cli.pki.import_unconfirmed: Certificate not used: check the notices above, then run again with --yes
cli.pki.imported: Own certificate saved; the running platform uses it within a minute.
cli.pki.remove_unconfirmed: Not removed: check the notices above, then run again with --yes
cli.pki.removed: Own certificate removed and the built-in CA in use again; the running platform switches within a minute.
cli.backup.done: Backup written to {path} (without the key file: back it up separately)
cli.seed.no_ca: No certificate found in CA file {file}
